genesis.44.p1.b1.text: Fill the men’s sacks with as much food as they can carry, and put each one’s silver in the mouth of his sack.

genesis.44.p1.b2.text: Put my cup, the silver one, in the mouth of the youngest one’s sack, along with the silver for his grain.

genesis.44.p1.b3.text: So the steward did as Joseph had instructed.

genesis.44.p1.b4.text: At daybreak, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.

genesis.44.p2.b1.text: Pursue the men at once, and when you overtake them, ask, … Why have you repaid good with evil?

genesis.44.p2.b2.text: Is this not the cup my master drinks from and uses for divination? What you have done is wicked!’”

genesis.44.p2.b3.text: We even brought back to you from the land of Canaan the silver we found in the mouths of our sacks. Why would we steal silver or gold from your master’s house?

genesis.44.p2.b4.text: But only the one who is found with the cup will be my slave, and the rest of you shall be free of blame.

genesis.44.p3.b1.text: The steward searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest

genesis.44.p3.b2.text: and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

genesis.44.p3.b3.text: Then they all tore their clothes, loaded their donkeys, and returned to the city.

genesis.44.p4.b1.text: When Judah and his brothers arrived at Joseph’s house, he was still there, and they fell to the ground before him.

genesis.44.p4.b2.text: What is this deed you have done? … Do you not know that a man like me can surely divine the truth?

genesis.44.p4.b3.text: God has exposed the iniquity of your servants. We are now my lord’s slaves—both we and the one who was found with the cup.

genesis.44.p4.b4.text: The man who was found with the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may return to your father in peace.

genesis.44.p5.b1.text: Sir, please let your servant speak personally to my lord. Do not be angry with your servant, for you are equal to Pharaoh himself.

genesis.44.p5.b2.text: My lord asked his servants, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’

genesis.44.p5.b3.text: The boy’s brother is dead. He is the only one of his mother’s sons left, and his father loves him.

genesis.44.p5.b4.text: But you said to your servants, ‘Unless your younger brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.’

genesis.44.p6.b1.text: Then our father said, ‘Go back and buy us some food.’

genesis.44.p6.b2.text: So if our younger brother is not with us, we cannot see the man.

genesis.44.p6.b3.text: When one of them was gone, I said: “Surely he has been torn to pieces.” And I have not seen him since.

genesis.44.p6.b4.text: … you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.

genesis.44.p7.b1.text: my father, whose life is wrapped up in the boy’s life

genesis.44.p7.b2.text: … sees that the boy is not with us, he will die.

genesis.44.p7.b3.text: ‘If I do not return him to you, I will bear the guilt before you, my father, all my life.’

genesis.44.p8.b1.text: Now please let your servant stay here as my lord’s slave in place of the boy.

genesis.44.p8.b2.text: Let him return with his brothers.

genesis.44.p9.b1.text: For how can I go back to my father without the boy?

genesis.44.p9.b2.text: I could not bear to see the misery that would overwhelm him.
